title: Don’t Let a Crypto Inheritance Get Stuck on the Blockchain
gist: US estate law treats crypto as a digital asset, so inheritance depends on custody: bank custodians like Schwab and Chase offer simple beneficiary forms, while Coinbase and PayPal need documents and a death certificate. Noncustodial wallets need a DIY plan, best done with an estate plan naming a fiduciary while keeping passwords out of the public will, for example in a safe-deposit box.

themes.theme: Legal status of crypto in US inheritance

insights.claim: In the US, cryptocurrency is treated as a digital asset rather than money under probate and estate law, and the law presumes a deceased person did not want private digital materials passed on unless they explicitly said so, leaving crypto in an awkward position for inheritance.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Legal friction around digital-asset inheritance creates a structural risk of crypto supply being stranded at holders' deaths.
insights.quote: In the US, cryptocurrency is considered a digital asset rather than money in terms of probate and estate law.

insights.claim: Holders of crypto who make no inheritance arrangements face a real possibility that their funds will die with them.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Unplanned self-custodied coins can become permanently inaccessible, effectively removing them from circulating supply.
insights.quote: if you do nothing, it's very possible those funds will die with you.

insights.claim: The Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act is the law that guides how digital inheritance is handled in most US states.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
entities: Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act
insights.so_what: This uniform act is the key legal framework governing access to inherited digital assets across most states.

themes.theme: Custodial vs noncustodial: the core divide

insights.claim: Options for transferring crypto at death or incapacitation split on whether assets are held by a custodian such as a bank or exchange, where transfer is typically much easier, or in a noncustodial wallet, which always requires a do-it-yourself solution.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Custody choice determines whether crypto wealth can pass through conventional estate channels.
insights.quote: Typically, transferring assets after death is much easier with a custodian, especially if it's a bank.

insights.claim: For crypto enthusiasts motivated by a distaste for the traditional banking system, using a noncustodial wallet that removes the middleman is essentially the whole point of holding crypto.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Ideological self-custody preference limits how much crypto wealth migrates to bank custodians despite inheritance advantages.

themes.theme: Banks and exchanges as crypto custodians

insights.claim: Charles Schwab and Chase offer crypto services and have experience transferring assets after death; Schwab houses crypto within brokerage accounts so a single brokerage beneficiary form also covers the crypto.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Large incumbent banks offering crypto with built-in beneficiary processes gain an edge for estate-conscious holders.
insights.quote: Signing a beneficiary form for a brokerage account applies to the crypto account as well. One and done.

insights.claim: Bank-held accounts are known to the bank, the government, and credit reporting bureaus, so avenues exist to find a deceased person's banked money, and being locked out of an online portal has no bearing on a beneficiary's ability to receive funds.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Discoverability and recoverability are a key value proposition of custodial crypto versus self-custody.

insights.claim: Cryptocurrency accounts are not FDIC-insured, even when held through a bank.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Bank custody of crypto does not carry deposit insurance protection.
insights.quote: Note that cryptocurrency accounts, even when held through a bank, are not FDIC-insured.

insights.claim: As of the article's writing, neither Coinbase nor PayPal has beneficiary forms, though both have a clear process requiring legal documents (executor status for PayPal, entitlement to inherit for Coinbase) plus a death certificate, making the process clunky but straightforward.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Lack of beneficiary forms at major crypto platforms is a product gap versus banks like Schwab.
insights.quote: Neither Coinbase nor PayPal have beneficiary forms as of this writing

insights.claim: Custodians' drawbacks include required ID that prevents anonymous holding, reporting of transactions to the federal government, and transaction fees that are usually a small percentage of each trade.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Tax reporting, KYC, and fees are the trade-offs pushing some holders toward self-custody.

insights.claim: With a noncustodial wallet, losing your cryptographic key means there is no company to appeal to, so being locked out while alive is game over.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Irrecoverable key loss is a permanent risk for self-custodied crypto wealth.

insights.so_what: Physical device failure is a tail risk for self-custodied assets with no recourse.

themes.theme: Building a DIY crypto inheritance plan

insights.claim: Reddit users' ideas for passing on crypto, such as email dead-man switches, printed instructions given to a trusted person, and splitting instructions across two people, could work but have obvious failure modes like email system failure or a trusted person dying alongside the holder.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Informal inheritance schemes are fragile, suggesting demand for more robust crypto estate tools.

insights.claim: The best option may be to put most inheritance instructions and the named fiduciary into an estate plan while omitting passwords, because a will is a public document; passwords can instead be kept in a bank safe-deposit box whose existence is listed in the will.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Practical estate structuring can keep self-custodied crypto recoverable without exposing keys.

insights.claim: A remaining flaw in any self-custody inheritance plan is that it cannot be dry-run without complete trust in the fiduciary, and something as simple as a fingerprint unlock could defeat it.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Untestable inheritance plans mean some share of self-custodied crypto will likely be lost.
insights.quote: Something as simple as needing your fingerprint to unlock a device could spell the end of your plan.

insights.claim: Some staunchly anti-capitalistic investors may object that putting crypto into an estate plan returns it to the realm of traditional law and governance, though the author counters that they will be dead.
insights.speaker: Jill Duffy
insights.so_what: Ideological resistance to formal estate planning may increase stranded crypto.
